newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia govt to seek confidence vote if EU missed.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia govt to seek confidence vote if EU missed.

text.p: Slovenian Premier Janez Drnovsek said on Thursday he would seek a vote of confidence if Slovenia failed to be included in the first round of EU expansion even after approving an accord with the bloc.

He said Slovenia had no chance of being included in the first round of expansion unless it ratified an association accord with the European Union, which was signed in June last year, by the end of July.

"If we change the constitution by July 15, ratify the EU agreement by the end of July and still not get included in the first round of the EU expansion I would ask the parliament to take a vote of confidence in the government," Drnovsek told a news conference.

Earlier in June Slovenia's Constitutional Court said the parliament needed to change the constitution in order to enable foreigners to buy land in the country before it could take a vote on whether to ratify the EU accord.
Drnovsek spoke just before leaving for Amsterdam, where he will attend the Friday meeting of the European Union with heads of aspiring member countries.
"In Amsterdam I expect to receive formal views on the EU expansion, an exact interpretation of the Amsterdam summit," he said.
The European Commission is expected to unveil on July 16 its advice to EU hopefuls on how suitable each is for EU entry.
Slovenia, Poland, the Czech Republic, Hungary, Slovakia, Romania, Bulgaria, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Cyprus and Turkey all hope to join the EU as soon as possible.

"I expect the first round will include at most five new members with Poland, the Czech Republic and Hungary being in the best position. Apart for a place for one Baltic state, probably Estonia, there is another place that Slovenia expects to get," Drnovsek added.
